## Summary

The worst hyperinflation on record. After a war that destroyed most of its industry and transport, and under Soviet occupation and reparations, Hungary financed the state with the printing press. In **July 1946 prices rose 4.19 × 10¹⁶ % in one month — they doubled every 15 hours** (H&K). The pengő was replaced on 1 August 1946 by the forint, at **400 octillion (4 × 10²⁹) pengő to 1**.

## Causes

- **Occupation and reparations.** The Soviet army lived off the country, and the armistice imposed
  reparations to the USSR, Czechoslovakia and Yugoslavia.
- **Deficit financed by the central bank.** With almost no tax base, the government paid with new
  money; the National Bank lent freely to the state and to firms.

## Timeline

- **Aug 1945** — monthly inflation crosses 50% (H&K start); 1,320 pengő per dollar.
- **Dec 1945** — 128,000 pengő per dollar.
- **1 Jan 1946** — the **adópengő** ("tax pengő") is introduced as an indexed unit of account for
  taxes and bank deposits, re-pegged to the pengő daily.
- **31 May 1946** — 4.2 × 10¹⁶ pengő per dollar.
- **9 Jul 1946** — adópengő tax bills become legal tender.
- **Jul 1946** — peak: 4.19 × 10¹⁶ % in the month, prices doubling every 15 hours (H&K);
  4.6 × 10³⁰ pengő per dollar on 10 July.
- **1 Aug 1946** — the **forint** replaces the pengő at 4 × 10²⁹ to 1.

## Life during it

- Prices were posted and changed during the day; at one stage the pengő lost 90% of its value in
  about four days (Wikipedia).
- Money was swept off the streets as worthless; people traded in goods, foreign currency and gold.
- Indexation (the adópengő) protected tax receipts and deposits for a while — then itself
  hyperinflated, because it was still printed to pay the state.

## The end

Prices stabilised immediately and the forint held its value for years.

## Lessons

- Indexing (adópengő) does not stop inflation; it only moves who bears it, until the indexed unit
  is printed too.
- Even the worst hyperinflation in history ended overnight once the new unit was limited and the
  state stopped paying with it.
